ov: Freshwater relatives of lobsters, also called crawfish or crawdads. They live in streams, swamps, ditches and paddy fields, and most can’t tolerate polluted water. They can eat almost anything, even grass, leaves and paper, but need a varied diet.

why.p: Kept as pets in freshwater aquariums.
why.et: Eaten worldwide, though only a small part of the body is eaten.

rg: North America, Europe and western Asia, East Asia, South America, Madagascar and Australasia. Most species live in south-eastern North America.
df: Living or decomposing plants and animals, and detritus.

cf.tip: Crayfish are the lobster’s freshwater relatives.

fx: “Crayfish” comes from the Old French escrevisse, altered to end in “fish”.
South-eastern North America has over 330 crayfish species, the most anywhere.

_cf.tip: Crayfish are the lobster’s freshwater relatives.
